variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: Apply the memory update before choosing the next subgoal. Each episode starts with A, press button: the initial scene has no held cube and remaining_targets is null. If remaining_targets is still null and no completed reveal is available, choose A. When remaining_targets is a nonempty list and the gripper is empty, choose B, pick up the highlighted cube, targeting any eligible cube represented in remaining_targets. The list order is a storage convention, not a required pickup order. Point at that cube's current center, allowing minor centroid wobble; do not point at the former white area or substitute another cube of the same color.  If the current scene shows a cube held after pickup, choose C, place the cube onto the table, even though that cube has already been removed from remaining_targets. After placement, an empty gripper and a nonempty remaining_targets list lead back to B for any eligible cube in that list; never pick up an already removed cube again. If pickup failed, retain the target and retry B. If placement failed and the cube remains held, retry C. If the target is temporarily occluded, use its stored table coordinate for B rather than switching targets. If remaining_targets is empty and the gripper is empty, the task is complete; no further pickup or button press is required. If nevertheless forced to select a menu option after completion, choose C as the non-pickup fallback. For other unmodeled situations, choose C if holding a cube, otherwise B at any eligible remaining target if one exists, otherwise A only when remaining_targets is null.

fields.name: remaining_targets
fields.description: Initialize to null when the incoming memory is empty. Inspect all execution frames provided at this decision, not just the final scene. If the incoming value is null and the frames show the button-press interval and white highlighted areas, associate each highlighted area with the cube immediately above or overlapping it and record that cube's table center as [y, x]. Deduplicate repeated sightings. Order targets by image columns from smaller x to larger x; cubes whose x coordinates differ by at most 10 pixels count as the same column and are ordered by increasing y. Once initialized, retain this list. If the supplied frames show a cube being grasped at a listed table location and subsequently lifted while held, remove that entry at this decision. Use its pre-lift table position to identify it, not its raised position. An unsuccessful closure or temporary disappearance is not sufficient for removal. Placement does not add an entry back. Keep stored coordinates unchanged despite occlusion or small visible centroid changes. An empty list means all revealed targets have been picked up; null means the reveal has not yet been recorded. e.g. [[63, 150]]
fields.annotation: The list of highlighted cubes not yet successfully picked up, represented by their table-center coordinates [y, x]. Before the button-reveal interval has been observed, use null rather than an empty list. At the decision immediately following the button press, populate the list by matching every white highlighted area seen during that interval to its cube; store cube centers, not highlight centers. Order targets by image columns from smaller x to larger x; cubes whose x coordinates differ by at most 10 pixels count as the same column and are ordered by increasing y. At each decision following a successful pickup, remove the picked cube. Do not remove a cube merely because a pickup was commanded, and do not restore it when placed down. Preserve remaining coordinates through occlusion and minor centroid wobble. Thus episode 6 has null, [[89, 146], [63, 150]], [[63, 150]], [[63, 150]]; episode 28 has null, [[64, 91]]; episode 38 has null, [[81, 125], [113, 120]], [[113, 120]], [[113, 120]]; episode 57 has null, [[84, 92]]; episode 98 has null, [[99, 104], [112, 146]], [[112, 146]], [[112, 146]]. e.g. [[63, 150]]

history.critique:
the policy prompt for subgoal
  The goal requires pressing the button and then picking up every highlighted cube, without specifying their order. After the reveal, the memory correctly retained all highlighted cube centers. However, choosing its first entry selected a red cube when the recording selected a blue cube. In another scene, it selected a blue cube both immediately after the reveal and after placement, whereas the recording selected the two highlighted red cubes first. Thus the first-entry rule fails SUFFICIENCY for predicting the recorded target, although its choices still satisfy the stated task. Remove the claim that the coordinate-sorted list defines the required pickup order, including that assumption in fallback rules. Treat the list as the remaining eligible targets: when the gripper is empty, choose B at an eligible cube's current center, or its stored center if occluded; when holding a cube, choose C. Retain the existing reveal, successful-pickup removal, placement, and retry rules. This repairs the task-level interpretation but does not establish exact recorded-choice prediction. The supplied evidence does not identify a general observable priority rule that predicts those choices. Exact trajectory matching therefore remains unresolved and requires an independently supported target-selection convention; it must not be presented as solved by adding an invented ordering rule.

refused
  The reports correctly identify that selecting the first stored target does not reproduce the recorded choices. Their proposed or implied target-priority fixes are not supported across the supplied scenes. Strictly increasing x would select the desired blue cube in the scene with two nearby image columns, but would still incorrectly select the blue cube before both red cubes in the three-target scene; it would also select a red cube before the recorded green cube in another scene. A fixed red-before-blue priority conflicts with the recorded blue-before-red choice. No instruction or demonstrated ordering establishes either convention. Consequently, do not add either priority, episode-specific exceptions, or a memory queue filled from future recorded pickups. Such a queue would require information unavailable during the reveal and would violate PREDICTABILITY. The existing remaining_targets field already contains every candidate needed later, and its reveal and removal transitions were correctly reproduced, so no change to either memory document is justified by these reports.

applied.refused: No memory changes or target-priority conventions are committed. The reported memory transitions were correct, and neither a spatial priority nor a color priority is supported across the reported scenes. Episode-specific exceptions and a queue derived from future recorded pickups would not provide a predictable runtime rule. These edits remove an unsupported task-order restriction; they do not resolve exact recorded-target prediction when multiple eligible targets remain.

history.critique:
refused
  Both reports concern choosing among multiple remembered highlighted cubes with an empty gripper. The goal required pressing the button and then picking up every highlighted cube, but specified no pickup order. After the reveal, the policy chose a highlighted green cube instead of the recorded red cube; after a placement, it chose a remaining highlighted green cube instead of the recorded blue cube. In both cases, remaining_targets correctly contained both the chosen and recorded objects, and the policy prompt for subgoal explicitly permitted either choice. These reports identify an unresolved SUFFICIENCY issue for predicting the exact recorded target, not missing historical information or an incorrect memory update. Neither report supplies evidence for a general target-selection rule, and the trajectories do not establish a consistent simple priority such as list order, image-column order, or forwardmost first. I am not passing on a prescribed red-first or blue-first tie-breaker, an episode-specific exception, or a memory field encoding the future recorded choice: those would invent a requirement or use information unavailable at runtime. No memory annotation or execution change is warranted. A justified exact-target correction requires an independently specified selection convention or additional evidence establishing one; the existing any-eligible-target rule remains consistent with the stated task.

applied.refused: No edits committed. This round supplies no supported target-selection convention and requests no concrete change. Both mismatches select eligible remembered targets, and all memory updates were correct. Adding a color or spatial priority, restoring first-entry selection, or adding episode-specific exceptions would invent an unsupported ordering and repeat the issue rejected in Round 1. Encoding future recorded choices in memory would violate runtime predictability. Retain the any-eligible-target rule; exact recorded-target prediction remains unresolved and requires an independently specified selection convention or evidence establishing one.

history.critique:
the policy prompt for subgoal
  When the button-reveal interval showed both a blue cube and a green cube highlighted, the final scene no longer showed the white areas. The correctly updated remaining_targets contained both cube centers, ordered with the green cube first. The policy selected that green cube, whereas the recorded action selected the blue cube. The rule allowing any eligible target therefore breaks SUFFICIENCY for predicting the recorded target; the highlight memory itself was sufficient and correctly updated. Replace the permission to choose any remaining target with a deterministic selection rule: when the gripper is empty, match remaining_targets to the cubes shown in the supplied observations; if both a blue and a green target remain, select the blue target before the green target. Otherwise select the first entry in remaining_targets. This preserves the observed first-target choices when the highlighted cubes have the same color, while resolving the observed blue-versus-green choice. Apply this selection rule everywhere the policy prompt currently permits any eligible target, including after placement and in its fallback rule. Remove the statement that list order is merely a storage convention with no pickup-order role: it is the default selection order, subordinate to the blue-before-green priority. Continue pointing at the selected cube's current center, or its stored table coordinate when occluded. Do not change the rules for recording highlights, removing successfully lifted cubes, retaining occluded targets, or placing a held cube.

applied.refused: No edits committed. The proposed blue-before-green priority is supported only by this round's single ambiguous choice, not by an independently established selection convention. Its first-entry fallback would restore the ordering rejected in Round 1, where list order failed to predict recorded choices. Applying these rules after placement and in fallbacks, and making storage order a pickup priority again, would therefore undo earlier corrections. The memory correctly retained both eligible targets; this mismatch supplies no evidence of missing historical information or an incorrect update. Retain the any-eligible-target rule and both memory documents unchanged. Exact recorded-target prediction remains unresolved and requires additional evidence establishing a general selection convention, rather than accumulating color-specific exceptions.

history.critique:
the policy prompt for subgoal
  The goal asks the robot to press the button and pick up all cubes revealed by white table highlights. After the reveal, and again after placing a successfully picked cube back down, the gripper was empty and remaining_targets correctly contained several eligible cube centers. The policy chose the eligible cube with the smallest image x, whereas the recorded choices selected the eligible cube with the largest image x, then the next-largest after that cube was removed. The existing permission to choose any eligible cube therefore breaks SUFFICIENCY for predicting the recorded target; the memory itself correctly preserves the required information and needs no change. Replace every permission to select any eligible remaining target, including the fallback rule, with a deterministic priority: when the gripper is empty and remaining_targets is nonempty, choose B for the remaining cube whose stored center has the largest x (the robot's leftmost eligible cube). For an exact x tie, choose the smaller stored y. Compare the stored coordinates, independently of the list's storage order, and point at the selected cube's current visible center, or its stored center if temporarily occluded. Remove the unrestricted any-eligible-target rule. Retain the existing reveal, successful-pickup removal, placement, retry, and completion rules; holding a cube still requires C before another pickup. This target priority accounts for both reported failures without adding memory.

applied.refused: No edits committed. The proposed largest-stored-x priority and smaller-y tie-breaker explain this round's choices but are not established as a general selection convention across rounds. Earlier reports likewise proposed local spatial or color priorities without evidence that they predict the other recorded choices. Replacing every any-eligible-target clause, including the fallback, would abandon the previously retained task-consistent rule on the strength of another local pattern; the exact-x tie-breaker has no reported support at all. Both selected and recorded cubes were eligible, and all memory updates were correct, so neither memory document needs changing. Retain the current policy prompts. Exact recorded-target prediction remains unresolved and requires an independently specified convention or evidence establishing a priority across the trajectories, rather than another round-specific ordering.

history.critique:
the policy prompt for subgoal
  After the button reveal, the goal required picking up every highlighted cube. In the failing situation, two red cubes had been highlighted, the highlights had disappeared, and the gripper was empty. The correctly updated remaining_targets list contained both cube centers, [[71, 140], [57, 155]]. The policy selected the first stored target, whereas the recorded action selected the cube at [57, 155]. The existing permission to choose any eligible target leaves the object selected by the next subgoal unsettled, breaking SUFFICIENCY; the memory itself retains all necessary information and needs no change. Replace every 'any eligible cube' or 'any eligible remaining target' pickup-selection rule with a deterministic rule: when the gripper is empty and remaining_targets is nonempty, choose B for the remaining target with the smallest stored y coordinate, breaking an exact y tie by the smallest stored x coordinate. This selects the target nearest the robot, not necessarily the first entry in storage order. Point at the selected cube's current visible center, or its stored table coordinate if occluded. Apply this same selection rule after the reveal, after placement, and in the general pickup fallback. Keep the existing successful-pickup removal, failed-pickup retention, and held-cube placement rules. Do not change the list's storage ordering or add a memory field for the selection preference.

Order targets by image columns from smaller x to larger x; cubes whose x coordinates differ by at most 10 pixels count as the same column and are ordered by increasing y. At each decision following a successful pickup, remove the picked cube. Do not remove a cube merely because a pickup was commanded, and do not restore it when placed down. Preserve remaining coordinates through occlusion and minor centroid wobble. Thus episode 6 has null, [[89, 146], [63, 150]], [[63, 150]], [[63, 150]]; episode 28 has null, [[64, 91]]; episode 38 has null, [[81, 125], [113, 120]], [[113, 120]], [[113, 120]]; episode 57 has null, [[84, 92]]; episode 98 has null, [[99, 104], [112, 146]], [[112, 146]], [[112, 146]]. e.g. [[63, 150]]

variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: Apply the memory update before choosing the next subgoal. Each episode starts with A, press button: the initial scene has no held cube and remaining_targets is null. If remaining_targets is still null and no completed reveal is available, choose A. When remaining_targets is a nonempty list and the gripper is empty, choose B, pick up the highlighted cube, targeting any eligible cube represented in remaining_targets. The list order is a storage convention, not a required pickup order. Point at that cube's current center, allowing minor centroid wobble; do not point at the former white area or substitute another cube of the same color.  If the current scene shows a cube held after pickup, choose C, place the cube onto the table, even though that cube has already been removed from remaining_targets. After placement, an empty gripper and a nonempty remaining_targets list lead back to B for any eligible cube in that list; never pick up an already removed cube again. If pickup failed, retain the target and retry B. If placement failed and the cube remains held, retry C. If the target is temporarily occluded, use its stored table coordinate for B rather than switching targets. If remaining_targets is empty and the gripper is empty, the task is complete; no further pickup or button press is required. If nevertheless forced to select a menu option after completion, choose C as the non-pickup fallback. For other unmodeled situations, choose C if holding a cube, otherwise B at any eligible remaining target if one exists, otherwise A only when remaining_targets is null.

fields.name: remaining_targets
fields.description: Initialize to null when the incoming memory is empty. Inspect all execution frames provided at this decision, not just the final scene. If the incoming value is null and the frames show the button-press interval and white highlighted areas, associate each highlighted area with the cube immediately above or overlapping it and record that cube's table center as [y, x]. Deduplicate repeated sightings. Order targets by image columns from smaller x to larger x; cubes whose x coordinates differ by at most 10 pixels count as the same column and are ordered by increasing y. Once initialized, retain this list. If the supplied frames show a cube being grasped at a listed table location and subsequently lifted while held, remove that entry at this decision. Use its pre-lift table position to identify it, not its raised position. An unsuccessful closure or temporary disappearance is not sufficient for removal. Placement does not add an entry back. Keep stored coordinates unchanged despite occlusion or small visible centroid changes. An empty list means all revealed targets have been picked up; null means the reveal has not yet been recorded. e.g. [[63, 150]]
